morphology_entries.iccc3_subgroup_name: Other and unspecified malignant gonadal tumors
morphology_entries.coding_note: Generated by build/generate_group10_entries.py from ICCC-2017.sqlite joined to icdo32.sqlite (build_inventory, group X), never transcribed from the REDCap option file or the Diagnostic Pathway document (contract §2). ICD-O-3.2 preferred term at /3 is 'Neoplasm, malignant'. The gonadal fallback: ICCC-2017 range 117 places 8000-8005 at C56.9 and C62 in Xe (D13). Imaging that shows a tumour, with no marker the report calls raised, is registered here at basis of diagnosis 2, and a note that states a malignant tumour at basis of diagnosis 1 (Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rule 5, p. 03; D4). The central nervous system and extragonadal trees refer the same findings to Groups III and XII. Emitted by g10_ovary and g10_testis (design D4, D13).

nodes.question: Answer each stain as the report states it.
nodes.hint: The report calls the tumour a germ cell tumour without naming its type. Answer 'Not done or not readable' for a stain the report does not mention. A tumour with more than one germ cell component is coded at the mixed germ cell tumour step instead. One yolk sac marker alone does not establish a yolk sac tumour: glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein and HNF1-beta each stain some teratomas (Siegmund 2023, p. 38; Rougemont 2018, p. 26). Human chorionic gonadotropin staining does not establish choriocarcinoma: it also stains the syncytiotrophoblastic cells found in seminoma (Siegmund 2023, p. 38).
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, each rule verified against the printed page. Siegmund SE, Mehra R, Acosta AM. Human Pathology 2023;133:32-55 (online 2022): Table 1, p. 34; KIT and D2-40, p. 36; CD30, OCT3/4, SOX2 and SOX17, p. 37; glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin and HNF1-beta, p. 38. Wu 2020, Tables 1-2. Rougemont 2018, pp. 26, 29, 31, 33-35. Contract rules 1-5 are kept; rules 1, 3 and 5 carry negatives the contract's table did not, so a seminoma with focal CD30, or an embryonal carcinoma with CD117 or D2-40, does not take the other's code. With OCT3/4 positive, a positive SOX17 decides the panel for the germinoma family whatever CD30 or SOX2 show (rule 4; a panel with OCT3/4, SOX17 and CD30 fires it), because SOX17 is negative in every embryonal carcinoma (Siegmund p. 37). Without SOX17, a panel positive for CD30 and for CD117 or D2-40 is coded 9064/3 unless SOX2 settles it (rule 2): rule 0 records it for CD117, the fallback for D2-40. Contract rules 6-8 (one yolk sac marker each) are replaced by two pairs, OCT3/4 not positive in each: glypican-3 with alpha-fetoprotein, and glypican-3 with nuclear HNF1-beta. A single yolk sac marker falls to the fallback. The pair alpha-fetoprotein with HNF1-beta is not built: no source on disk reports the two stains on the same tumours (Rougemont did not stain alpha-fetoprotein, p. 28; Siegmund p. 38 compares their accuracy, not their co-expression). Residual risk, teratoma: glypican-3 stains 20-38% and tissue alpha-fetoprotein 0-27% of teratomas (Siegmund p. 38); nuclear HNF1-beta stains enteric-type teratoma glands in 11/16 (Rougemont p. 26; Table 5, p. 33); Wu Tables 1-2 found glypican-3 in 1/10 and alpha-fetoprotein in 2/10 mature teratomas, weak and in 2-3% of cells. No source reports how often a teratoma expresses both markers of a pair; one that does is coded 9071/3. Residual risk, choriocarcinoma: OCT3/4 negative and glypican-3 positive in 33-100% (Table 1, p. 34; p. 38); each pair needs a second marker the sources report choriocarcinoma rarely or never shows (alpha-fetoprotein, p. 38; nuclear HNF1-beta, Rougemont p. 26). SALL4 is declared and asked by no rule: it marks germ cell lineage, not type (Siegmund p. 36). Choriocarcinoma is not coded from immunohistochemistry (contract §4.2). Fallback 9064/3 per D2.

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and SOX2 are positive and SOX17 is not: the embryonal carcinoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, p. 37). Recorded as Embryonal carcinoma, NOS (9070/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 2. Siegmund 2023 p. 37 (Nonaka): diffuse SOX2 with negative SOX17 in 100% of embryonal carcinomas; diffuse SOX17 with negative SOX2 in 100% of seminomas. SOX2 in teratoma epithelium (up to 81%) is excluded by OCT3/4, which teratoma lacks (Table 1, p. 34). Listed first: it emits rule 1's code, and above rule 0 it keeps SOX2 asked before rule 0 can settle.

Recorded as Germinoma (9064/3): ICD-O-3.2 files Germ cell tumor, NOS under this number, so the record does not assert that a germinoma was diagnosed.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 0, after rule 2 and ahead of rule 1, so the flow asks CD117 before rule 1 can settle and SOX2 before rule 0 can. The engine counts an unasked negative marker as off and stops at the first satisfied rule, asking only about rules above it, so without this rule a seminoma with focal CD30 and a positive CD117 the clerk was never asked about was coded 9070/3. It records what the node's fallback records for the same panel; SOX2 and SOX17 negative keep rules 2 and 4 deciding when either is positive. Siegmund 2023 p. 37: CD30+/KIT- is 100% specific for embryonal carcinoma and CD30-/KIT+ for seminoma (Leroy).

resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 1. Siegmund 2023 p. 37: CD30 stains embryonal carcinoma (83-100%) and focally stains 0-50% of seminomas; CD30+/KIT- is 100% specific for embryonal carcinoma (Leroy). OCT3/4 marks seminoma and embryonal carcinoma (100% each, p. 37). negative CD117 and SOX17: added to the contract's rule, so a seminoma with focal CD30 is not coded embryonal carcinoma. SOX17 is negative in 100% of embryonal carcinomas (Nonaka, p. 37).

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and CD117 are positive and CD30 is not: the seminoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, pp. 36-37). Dysgerminoma, seminoma and germinoma are one tumour under three names (Moch 2022, p. 464), and the name this site uses is recorded. Recorded as Germinoma (9064/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 3. Siegmund 2023 p. 36: KIT stains 88-100% of seminomas; focal cytoplasmic KIT occurs in 32-44% of non-seminomatous tumours. p. 37: CD30-/KIT+ is 100% specific for seminoma (Leroy). negative CD30: added to the contract's rule for the same reason as rule 1. Family code by site, D3.

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and SOX17 are positive: the seminoma pattern. Embryonal carcinoma does not express SOX17 (Siegmund 2023, p. 37). Dysgerminoma, seminoma and germinoma are one tumour under three names (Moch 2022, p. 464), and the name this site uses is recorded. Recorded as Germinoma (9064/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 4. Siegmund 2023 p. 37 (Nonaka): SOX17 diffuse in 100% of seminomas, negative in 100% of embryonal carcinomas and in choriocarcinoma; variable in yolk sac tumour and teratoma, both OCT3/4 negative (Table 1, p. 34). No CD30 negative: a panel with OCT3/4, SOX17 and CD30 positive fires this rule (rule 1 requires SOX17 not positive), because SOX17 is negative in every embryonal carcinoma and CD30 focally stains up to half of seminomas (p. 37).

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and D2-40 are positive and CD30 is not: the seminoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, pp. 36-37). Dysgerminoma, seminoma and germinoma are one tumour under three names (Moch 2022, p. 464), and the name this site uses is recorded. Recorded as Germinoma (9064/3).

Siegmund 2023 p. 36: D2-40 strongly stains up to 100% of seminomas; embryonal carcinoma stains in 0-69%, focally. negative CD30: added to the contract's rule, so focal D2-40 in an embryonal carcinoma does not read as seminoma. p. 37: KIT/D2-40/SOX17 mark seminoma, CD30/SOX2 embryonal carcinoma.

resolution_logic.reason: Glypican-3 and alpha-fetoprotein both stain the tumour and OCT3/4 is not positive: the yolk sac tumour pattern (Siegmund 2023, p. 38; Wu 2020, Tables 1-2). Recorded as Yolk sac tumor, NOS (9071/3).

Siegmund 2023 p. 38: glypican-3 in 100% of yolk sac tumours and tissue alpha-fetoprotein in 55-100%; a subset of yolk sac tumours co-expresses alpha-fetoprotein and glypican-3 (Nogales). Choriocarcinoma, glypican-3 positive in 33-100%, is rarely alpha-fetoprotein positive (p. 38; Table 1, p. 34). Wu P, et al. Pediatr Surg Int 2020 (doi:10.1007/s00383-020-04652-w; the PDF prints no page numbers), Tables 1-2: alpha-fetoprotein 21/22 and glypican-3 22/22 paediatric yolk sac tumours. OCT3/4 negative in yolk sac tumour, Table 1, p. 34.

resolution_logic.reason: Glypican-3 and nuclear HNF1-beta are positive and OCT3/4 is not: the yolk sac tumour pattern (Rougemont 2018, Table 2, p. 29). Recorded as Yolk sac tumor, NOS (9071/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 7. Rougemont AL, Tille JC. Human Pathology 2018;81:26-36: Table 2, p. 29, glypican-3 positive in 42 of the 44 nuclear HNF1-beta positive yolk sac components it lists; p. 34, glypican-3 positive in 43/45; p. 35, recommends a panel combining SALL4, HNF1-beta, glypican-3 and OCT4. nodes.question: Answer each stain as the report states it.
nodes.hint: The report calls the tumour a germ cell tumour without naming its type. Answer 'Not done or not readable' for a stain the report does not mention. A tumour with more than one germ cell component is coded at the mixed germ cell tumour step instead. One yolk sac marker alone does not establish a yolk sac tumour: glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein and HNF1-beta each stain some teratomas (Siegmund 2023, p. 38; Rougemont 2018, p. 26). Human chorionic gonadotropin staining does not establish choriocarcinoma: it also stains the syncytiotrophoblastic cells found in seminoma (Siegmund 2023, p. 38).
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, each rule verified against the printed page. Siegmund SE, Mehra R, Acosta AM. Human Pathology 2023;133:32-55 (online 2022): Table 1, p. 34; KIT and D2-40, p. 36; CD30, OCT3/4, SOX2 and SOX17, p. 37; glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin and HNF1-beta, p. 38. Wu 2020, Tables 1-2. Rougemont 2018, pp. 26, 29, 31, 33-35. Contract rules 1-5 are kept; rules 1, 3 and 5 carry negatives the contract's table did not, so a seminoma with focal CD30, or an embryonal carcinoma with CD117 or D2-40, does not take the other's code. With OCT3/4 positive, a positive SOX17 decides the panel for the germinoma family whatever CD30 or SOX2 show (rule 4; a panel with OCT3/4, SOX17 and CD30 fires it), because SOX17 is negative in every embryonal carcinoma (Siegmund p. 37). Without SOX17, a panel positive for CD30 and for CD117 or D2-40 is coded 9064/3 unless SOX2 settles it (rule 2): rule 0 records it for CD117, the fallback for D2-40. Contract rules 6-8 (one yolk sac marker each) are replaced by two pairs, OCT3/4 not positive in each: glypican-3 with alpha-fetoprotein, and glypican-3 with nuclear HNF1-beta. A single yolk sac marker falls to the fallback. The pair alpha-fetoprotein with HNF1-beta is not built: no source on disk reports the two stains on the same tumours (Rougemont did not stain alpha-fetoprotein, p. 28; Siegmund p. 38 compares their accuracy, not their co-expression). Residual risk, teratoma: glypican-3 stains 20-38% and tissue alpha-fetoprotein 0-27% of teratomas (Siegmund p. 38); nuclear HNF1-beta stains enteric-type teratoma glands in 11/16 (Rougemont p. 26; Table 5, p. 33); Wu Tables 1-2 found glypican-3 in 1/10 and alpha-fetoprotein in 2/10 mature teratomas, weak and in 2-3% of cells. No source reports how often a teratoma expresses both markers of a pair; one that does is coded 9071/3. Residual risk, choriocarcinoma: OCT3/4 negative and glypican-3 positive in 33-100% (Table 1, p. 34; p. 38); each pair needs a second marker the sources report choriocarcinoma rarely or never shows (alpha-fetoprotein, p. 38; nuclear HNF1-beta, Rougemont p. 26). SALL4 is declared and asked by no rule: it marks germ cell lineage, not type (Siegmund p. 36). Choriocarcinoma is not coded from immunohistochemistry (contract §4.2). Fallback 9064/3 per D2.

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and SOX2 are positive and SOX17 is not: the embryonal carcinoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, p. 37). Recorded as Embryonal carcinoma, NOS (9070/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 2. Siegmund 2023 p. 37 (Nonaka): diffuse SOX2 with negative SOX17 in 100% of embryonal carcinomas; diffuse SOX17 with negative SOX2 in 100% of seminomas. SOX2 in teratoma epithelium (up to 81%) is excluded by OCT3/4, which teratoma lacks (Table 1, p. 34). Listed first: it emits rule 1's code, and above rule 0 it keeps SOX2 asked before rule 0 can settle.

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4, CD30 and CD117 are all positive, and SOX2 and SOX17 are not: the panel matches neither the embryonal carcinoma pattern (CD30 without CD117) nor the seminoma pattern (CD117 without CD30) (Siegmund 2023, p. 37), so it does not establish the germ cell tumour's type. Recorded as Germinoma (9064/3): ICD-O-3.2 files Germ cell tumor, NOS under this number, so the record does not assert that a germinoma was diagnosed.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 0, after rule 2 and ahead of rule 1, so the flow asks CD117 before rule 1 can settle and SOX2 before rule 0 can. The engine counts an unasked negative marker as off and stops at the first satisfied rule, asking only about rules above it, so without this rule a seminoma with focal CD30 and a positive CD117 the clerk was never asked about was coded 9070/3. It records what the node's fallback records for the same panel; SOX2 and SOX17 negative keep rules 2 and 4 deciding when either is positive. Siegmund 2023 p. 37: CD30+/KIT- is 100% specific for embryonal carcinoma and CD30-/KIT+ for seminoma (Leroy).

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and CD30 are positive, and the seminoma markers CD117 and SOX17 are not: the embryonal carcinoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, p. 37). Recorded as Embryonal carcinoma, NOS (9070/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 1. Siegmund 2023 p. 37: CD30 stains embryonal carcinoma (83-100%) and focally stains 0-50% of seminomas; CD30+/KIT- is 100% specific for embryonal carcinoma (Leroy). OCT3/4 marks seminoma and embryonal carcinoma (100% each, p. 37). negative CD117 and SOX17: added to the contract's rule, so a seminoma with focal CD30 is not coded embryonal carcinoma. SOX17 is negative in 100% of embryonal carcinomas (Nonaka, p. 37).

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and CD117 are positive and CD30 is not: the seminoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, pp. 36-37). Dysgerminoma, seminoma and germinoma are one tumour under three names (Moch 2022, p. 464), and the name this site uses is recorded. Recorded as Dysgerminoma (9060/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 3. Siegmund 2023 p. 36: KIT stains 88-100% of seminomas; focal cytoplasmic KIT occurs in 32-44% of non-seminomatous tumours. p. 37: CD30-/KIT+ is 100% specific for seminoma (Leroy). negative CD30: added to the contract's rule for the same reason as rule 1. Family code by site, D3.

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and SOX17 are positive: the seminoma pattern. Embryonal carcinoma does not express SOX17 (Siegmund 2023, p. 37). Dysgerminoma, seminoma and germinoma are one tumour under three names (Moch 2022, p. 464), and the name this site uses is recorded. Recorded as Dysgerminoma (9060/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 4. Siegmund 2023 p. 37 (Nonaka): SOX17 diffuse in 100% of seminomas, negative in 100% of embryonal carcinomas and in choriocarcinoma; variable in yolk sac tumour and teratoma, both OCT3/4 negative (Table 1, p. 34). No CD30 negative: a panel with OCT3/4, SOX17 and CD30 positive fires this rule (rule 1 requires SOX17 not positive), because SOX17 is negative in every embryonal carcinoma and CD30 focally stains up to half of seminomas (p. 37).

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and D2-40 are positive and CD30 is not: the seminoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, pp. 36-37). Dysgerminoma, seminoma and germinoma are one tumour under three names (Moch 2022, p. 464), and the name this site uses is recorded. Recorded as Dysgerminoma (9060/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 5. Siegmund 2023 p. 36: D2-40 strongly stains up to 100% of seminomas; embryonal carcinoma stains in 0-69%, focally. negative CD30: added to the contract's rule, so focal D2-40 in an embryonal carcinoma does not read as seminoma. p. 37: KIT/D2-40/SOX17 mark seminoma, CD30/SOX2 embryonal carcinoma.

resolution_logic.reason: Glypican-3 and alpha-fetoprotein both stain the tumour and OCT3/4 is not positive: the yolk sac tumour pattern (Siegmund 2023, p. 38; Wu 2020, Tables 1-2). Recorded as Yolk sac tumor, NOS (9071/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 6. Siegmund 2023 p. 38: glypican-3 in 100% of yolk sac tumours and tissue alpha-fetoprotein in 55-100%; a subset of yolk sac tumours co-expresses alpha-fetoprotein and glypican-3 (Nogales). Choriocarcinoma, glypican-3 positive in 33-100%, is rarely alpha-fetoprotein positive (p. 38; Table 1, p. 34). Wu P, et al. Pediatr Surg Int 2020 (doi:10.1007/s00383-020-04652-w; the PDF prints no page numbers), Tables 1-2: alpha-fetoprotein 21/22 and glypican-3 22/22 paediatric yolk sac tumours. OCT3/4 negative in yolk sac tumour, Table 1, p. 34.

resolution_logic.reason: Glypican-3 and nuclear HNF1-beta are positive and OCT3/4 is not: the yolk sac tumour pattern (Rougemont 2018, Table 2, p. 29). Recorded as Yolk sac tumor, NOS (9071/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 7. Rougemont AL, Tille JC. Human Pathology 2018;81:26-36: Table 2, p. 29, glypican-3 positive in 42 of the 44 nuclear HNF1-beta positive yolk sac components it lists; p. 34, glypican-3 positive in 43/45; p. 35, recommends a panel combining SALL4, HNF1-beta, glypican-3 and OCT4. Choriocarcinoma shows cytoplasmic HNF1-beta only, never nuclear (p. 26; Table 5, p. 33), so the nuclear stain excludes it. p. 31: every yolk sac tumour SALL4 positive and OCT4 negative.

decision_trees.tree_label: Germ cell and sex cord-stromal tumours of the testis (C62.0-C62.9; ICCC-3 Xc, Xd and Xe, behaviour 3 only) - the common evidence and germ cell nodes, with behaviour exclusions for benign, borderline and in situ lesions

nodes.question: What is in the file for this tumour?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A pathology report on a biopsy or resection counts as histology. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue: pick from the other tiers.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: five evidence tiers. Every Group X tree carries the same tiers; the router's site capture chose this tree. A tier a Lab Report can join routes through a laboratory screen when Lab Report is ticked (registrar, 6 October 2026).

nodes.hint: No imaging report, marker result or tissue report is in the file. A note alone never establishes a germ cell tumour's type.

nodes.question: No tissue is in the file. What do the imaging report and the marker results show?
nodes.hint: Use the report's own words. The value must be called raised against the laboratory's range for the patient's age; a newborn's alpha-fetoprotein is high without a tumour. Each coded option also needs the diagnosis it names (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, Table 4).
nodes.coding_note: D4. The report's own statement against the age-specific range is read; nothing is re-gated numerically. Visser Table 4 registers a tumour the file calls a germ cell tumour (9064/3, 9065/3) or choriocarcinoma (9100/3); each coded label states that condition.

options.reason: Recorded as Germ cell tumor, nonseminomatous (9065/3) at basis of diagnosis 4. A germ cell tumour shown on imaging with a raised alpha-fetoprotein is registered to this code without tissue (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, Table 4). The marker does not name the histological type; a histology report gives it.
options.coding_note: D4. Visser Table 4, p. 06; rule 6, p. 05 (basis 4 needs a clinical investigation showing the tumour). The pathway's 9071/3 for a raised alpha-fetoprotein is not built: it records a histology no one saw.

options.label: Imaging shows a tumour and the report calls human chorionic gonadotropin raised; alpha-fetoprotein is normal or not measured; the file calls it a germ cell tumour
options.reason: Recorded as Germinoma (9064/3) at basis of diagnosis 4. ICD-O-3.2 files Germ cell tumor, NOS under this number, and a germ cell tumour with a raised human chorionic gonadotropin is registered to it without tissue (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, Table 4). The record does not assert that a germinoma was diagnosed; a histology report gives the type.
options.coding_note: D2, D4. Visser Table 4, p. 06.

options.label: Imaging shows a tumour and a marker is raised, but the file does not call it a germ cell tumour or choriocarcinoma

options.coding_note: evidence_tests stays Imaging and Tumour markers.

options.label: A marker is raised, but the imaging shows no tumour
options.reason: A raised tumour marker is not registered unless a clinical investigation shows the tumour (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 6).

nodes.question: What does the histology report call the tumour?
nodes.hint: Use the report's own term for the tumour.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.3. Moch H, et al. European Urology 2022;82(5):458-468, Table 3, pp. 464-465, is the testis baseline.

options.label: Seminoma
options.reason: Recorded as Seminoma, NOS (9061/3).
options.upgrade_path: Immunohistochemistry, where the report does not describe it, confirms the germ cell type the report names; it does not change this code.
options.recognition_aid: Reports describe sheets of large, uniform cells divided into lobules by thin fibrous septa that hold lymphocytes.

options.label: Seminoma, anaplastic or with a high mitotic index
options.reason: Recorded as Seminoma, anaplastic (9062/3). ICD-O-3.2 gives it the synonym Seminoma with high mitotic index.
options.recognition_aid: Reports describe a seminoma with many dividing cells (mitoses).

options.label: Spermatocytic tumour
options.reason: Recorded as Spermatocytic seminoma (9063/3). ICD-O-3.2 gives it the synonym Spermatocytic tumor.
options.coding_note: D3. Moch 2022 Table 3, p. 464.
options.recognition_aid: Reports describe nodules of three kinds of cell: small cells like lymphocytes, medium-sized round cells and giant cells.

options.label: Dysgerminoma
options.reason: Recorded as Dysgerminoma (9060/3).
options.upgrade_path: Immunohistochemistry, where the report does not describe it, confirms the germ cell type the report names; it does not change this code.
options.recognition_aid: Reports describe sheets of large, uniform cells divided into lobules by thin fibrous septa that hold lymphocytes.

options.label: Germinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Germinoma (9064/3). A report that uses the term germinoma is coded as written; dysgerminoma is 9060/3.
options.upgrade_path: Immunohistochemistry, where the report does not describe it, confirms the germ cell type the report names; it does not change this code.
options.recognition_aid: Reports describe sheets of large, uniform cells divided into lobules by thin fibrous septa that hold lymphocytes.

options.label: A teratoma, dermoid cyst or epidermoid cyst
options.recognition_aid: Reports describe several kinds of tissue side by side, such as skin with hair, teeth, cartilage, bone, glands, brain (glial) tissue or thyroid.

options.label: Embryonal carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Embryonal carcinoma, NOS (9070/3).
options.upgrade_path: Immunohistochemistry, where the report does not describe it, confirms the germ cell type the report names; it does not change this code.
options.recognition_aid: Reports describe solid, papillary or gland-like growth of poorly differentiated cells, usually markedly atypical, with prominent nucleoli and frequent mitoses. A report that says infantile embryonal carcinoma or polyembryonal embryonal carcinoma is not this option: ICD-O-3.2 lists those under the yolk sac tumour and the polyembryoma.

options.label: Polyembryoma (or embryonal carcinoma, polyembryonal type)
options.reason: Recorded as Polyembryoma (9072/3).
options.recognition_aid: Reports describe embryoid bodies: embryonal carcinoma and yolk sac tumour closely intermixed.

options.label: Yolk sac tumour, prepubertal or postpubertal type (or infantile embryonal carcinoma)
options.reason: Recorded as Yolk sac tumor, NOS (9071/3). WHO 2022 codes both types 9071/3 (Moch 2022, Table 3, p. 464).
options.upgrade_path: Immunohistochemistry, where the report does not describe it, confirms the germ cell type the report names; it does not change this code.
options.recognition_aid: Reports often describe several growth patterns in one tumour, most often microcystic or reticular, with hyaline globules and Schiller-Duval bodies.

options.label: Choriocarcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Choriocarcinoma, NOS (9100/3).
options.recognition_aid: Reports describe a haemorrhagic tumour of two cell types: single-nucleus trophoblast cells rimmed by large multinucleated syncytiotrophoblast cells.

options.label: Mixed germ cell tumour — more than one germ cell component

nodes.question: Answer each stain as the report states it.
nodes.hint: The report calls the tumour a germ cell tumour without naming its type. Answer 'Not done or not readable' for a stain the report does not mention. A tumour with more than one germ cell component is coded at the mixed germ cell tumour step instead. One yolk sac marker alone does not establish a yolk sac tumour: glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein and HNF1-beta each stain some teratomas (Siegmund 2023, p. 38; Rougemont 2018, p. 26). Human chorionic gonadotropin staining does not establish choriocarcinoma: it also stains the syncytiotrophoblastic cells found in seminoma (Siegmund 2023, p. 38).
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, each rule verified against the printed page. Siegmund SE, Mehra R, Acosta AM. Human Pathology 2023;133:32-55 (online 2022): Table 1, p. 34; KIT and D2-40, p. 36; CD30, OCT3/4, SOX2 and SOX17, p. 37; glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin and HNF1-beta, p. 38. Wu 2020, Tables 1-2. Rougemont 2018, pp. 26, 29, 31, 33-35. Contract rules 1-5 are kept; rules 1, 3 and 5 carry negatives the contract's table did not, so a seminoma with focal CD30, or an embryonal carcinoma with CD117 or D2-40, does not take the other's code. With OCT3/4 positive, a positive SOX17 decides the panel for the germinoma family whatever CD30 or SOX2 show (rule 4; a panel with OCT3/4, SOX17 and CD30 fires it), because SOX17 is negative in every embryonal carcinoma (Siegmund p. 37). Without SOX17, a panel positive for CD30 and for CD117 or D2-40 is coded 9064/3 unless SOX2 settles it (rule 2): rule 0 records it for CD117, the fallback for D2-40. Contract rules 6-8 (one yolk sac marker each) are replaced by two pairs, OCT3/4 not positive in each: glypican-3 with alpha-fetoprotein, and glypican-3 with nuclear HNF1-beta. A single yolk sac marker falls to the fallback. The pair alpha-fetoprotein with HNF1-beta is not built: no source on disk reports the two stains on the same tumours (Rougemont did not stain alpha-fetoprotein, p. 28; Siegmund p. 38 compares their accuracy, not their co-expression). Residual risk, teratoma: glypican-3 stains 20-38% and tissue alpha-fetoprotein 0-27% of teratomas (Siegmund p. 38); nuclear HNF1-beta stains enteric-type teratoma glands in 11/16 (Rougemont p. 26; Table 5, p. 33); Wu Tables 1-2 found glypican-3 in 1/10 and alpha-fetoprotein in 2/10 mature teratomas, weak and in 2-3% of cells. No source reports how often a teratoma expresses both markers of a pair; one that does is coded 9071/3. Residual risk, choriocarcinoma: OCT3/4 negative and glypican-3 positive in 33-100% (Table 1, p. 34; p. 38); each pair needs a second marker the sources report choriocarcinoma rarely or never shows (alpha-fetoprotein, p. 38; nuclear HNF1-beta, Rougemont p. 26). SALL4 is declared and asked by no rule: it marks germ cell lineage, not type (Siegmund p. 36). Choriocarcinoma is not coded from immunohistochemistry (contract §4.2). Fallback 9064/3 per D2.

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and SOX2 are positive and SOX17 is not: the embryonal carcinoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, p. 37). Recorded as Embryonal carcinoma, NOS (9070/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 2. Siegmund 2023 p. 37 (Nonaka): diffuse SOX2 with negative SOX17 in 100% of embryonal carcinomas; diffuse SOX17 with negative SOX2 in 100% of seminomas. SOX2 in teratoma epithelium (up to 81%) is excluded by OCT3/4, which teratoma lacks (Table 1, p. 34). Listed first: it emits rule 1's code, and above rule 0 it keeps SOX2 asked before rule 0 can settle.

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4, CD30 and CD117 are all positive, and SOX2 and SOX17 are not: the panel matches neither the embryonal carcinoma pattern (CD30 without CD117) nor the seminoma pattern (CD117 without CD30) (Siegmund 2023, p. 37), so it does not establish the germ cell tumour's type. Recorded as Germinoma (9064/3): ICD-O-3.2 files Germ cell tumor, NOS under this number, so the record does not assert that a germinoma was diagnosed.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 0, after rule 2 and ahead of rule 1, so the flow asks CD117 before rule 1 can settle and SOX2 before rule 0 can. The engine counts an unasked negative marker as off and stops at the first satisfied rule, asking only about rules above it, so without this rule a seminoma with focal CD30 and a positive CD117 the clerk was never asked about was coded 9070/3. It records what the node's fallback records for the same panel; SOX2 and SOX17 negative keep rules 2 and 4 deciding when either is positive. Siegmund 2023 p. 37: CD30+/KIT- is 100% specific for embryonal carcinoma and CD30-/KIT+ for seminoma (Leroy).

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and CD30 are positive, and the seminoma markers CD117 and SOX17 are not: the embryonal carcinoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, p. 37). Recorded as Embryonal carcinoma, NOS (9070/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 1. Siegmund 2023 p. 37: CD30 stains embryonal carcinoma (83-100%) and focally stains 0-50% of seminomas; CD30+/KIT- is 100% specific for embryonal carcinoma (Leroy). OCT3/4 marks seminoma and embryonal carcinoma (100% each, p. 37). negative CD117 and SOX17: added to the contract's rule, so a seminoma with focal CD30 is not coded embryonal carcinoma. SOX17 is negative in 100% of embryonal carcinomas (Nonaka, p. 37).

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and CD117 are positive and CD30 is not: the seminoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, pp. 36-37). Dysgerminoma, seminoma and germinoma are one tumour under three names (Moch 2022, p. 464), and the name this site uses is recorded. Recorded as Seminoma, NOS (9061/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 3. Siegmund 2023 p. 36: KIT stains 88-100% of seminomas; focal cytoplasmic KIT occurs in 32-44% of non-seminomatous tumours. p. 37: CD30-/KIT+ is 100% specific for seminoma (Leroy). negative CD30: added to the contract's rule for the same reason as rule 1. Family code by site, D3.

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and SOX17 are positive: the seminoma pattern. Embryonal carcinoma does not express SOX17 (Siegmund 2023, p. 37). Dysgerminoma, seminoma and germinoma are one tumour under three names (Moch 2022, p. 464), and the name this site uses is recorded. Recorded as Seminoma, NOS (9061/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 4. Siegmund 2023 p. 37 (Nonaka): SOX17 diffuse in 100% of seminomas, negative in 100% of embryonal carcinomas and in choriocarcinoma; variable in yolk sac tumour and teratoma, both OCT3/4 negative (Table 1, p. 34). No CD30 negative: a panel with OCT3/4, SOX17 and CD30 positive fires this rule (rule 1 requires SOX17 not positive), because SOX17 is negative in every embryonal carcinoma and CD30 focally stains up to half of seminomas (p. 37).

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and D2-40 are positive and CD30 is not: the seminoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, pp. 36-37). Dysgerminoma, seminoma and germinoma are one tumour under three names (Moch 2022, p. 464), and the name this site uses is recorded. Recorded as Seminoma, NOS (9061/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 5. Siegmund 2023 p. 36: D2-40 strongly stains up to 100% of seminomas; embryonal carcinoma stains in 0-69%, focally. negative CD30: added to the contract's rule, so focal D2-40 in an embryonal carcinoma does not read as seminoma. p. 37: KIT/D2-40/SOX17 mark seminoma, CD30/SOX2 embryonal carcinoma.

resolution_logic.reason: Glypican-3 and alpha-fetoprotein both stain the tumour and OCT3/4 is not positive: the yolk sac tumour pattern (Siegmund 2023, p. 38; Wu 2020, Tables 1-2). Recorded as Yolk sac tumor, NOS (9071/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 6. Siegmund 2023 p. 38: glypican-3 in 100% of yolk sac tumours and tissue alpha-fetoprotein in 55-100%; a subset of yolk sac tumours co-expresses alpha-fetoprotein and glypican-3 (Nogales). Choriocarcinoma, glypican-3 positive in 33-100%, is rarely alpha-fetoprotein positive (p. 38; Table 1, p. 34). Wu P, et al. Pediatr Surg Int 2020 (doi:10.1007/s00383-020-04652-w; the PDF prints no page numbers), Tables 1-2: alpha-fetoprotein 21/22 and glypican-3 22/22 paediatric yolk sac tumours. OCT3/4 negative in yolk sac tumour, Table 1, p. 34.

resolution_logic.reason: Glypican-3 and nuclear HNF1-beta are positive and OCT3/4 is not: the yolk sac tumour pattern (Rougemont 2018, Table 2, p. 29). Recorded as Yolk sac tumor, NOS (9071/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 7. Rougemont AL, Tille JC. Human Pathology 2018;81:26-36: Table 2, p. 29, glypican-3 positive in 42 of the 44 nuclear HNF1-beta positive yolk sac components it lists; p. 34, glypican-3 positive in 43/45; p. 35, recommends a panel combining SALL4, HNF1-beta, glypican-3 and OCT4. Choriocarcinoma shows cytoplasmic HNF1-beta only, never nuclear (p. 26; Table 5, p. 33), so the nuclear stain excludes it. p. 31: every yolk sac tumour SALL4 positive and OCT4 negative.

nodes.question: What does the referral letter or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: No imaging report, marker result or tissue report is in the file. A note alone never establishes a germ cell tumour's type.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rules 4 and 5, p. 03: 8000/3 at basis 1 when cancer is at least probable. 8000/3 is Group X only at the gonads (ICCC-2017 range 117); elsewhere the branch refers (D4). Evidence context 'referral': reached with evidence_tests [].

options.label: The note states a malignant tumour as the diagnosis, or as probable
options.reason: A diagnosis resting on clinical information alone is registered with the unspecified code (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 5). ICCC-3 places Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) in Group X only at the ovary and testis. At the sacrococcygeal region, mediastinum and retroperitoneum it is a Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms) code; at the liver, kidney or bone it belongs to Group VII, VI or VIII. Code the case from that group's tree.

options.label: The note says only possible or suspected
options.reason: Cancer is only possible on this evidence. Under the European registry rules a case that is only possibly cancer is not registered without pathology (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4).

options.label: An imaging report is in the file after all

nodes.question: Answer each stain as the report states it.
nodes.hint: The report calls the tumour a germ cell tumour without naming its type. Answer 'Not done or not readable' for a stain the report does not mention. A tumour with more than one germ cell component is coded at the mixed germ cell tumour step instead. One yolk sac marker alone does not establish a yolk sac tumour: glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein and HNF1-beta each stain some teratomas (Siegmund 2023, p. 38; Rougemont 2018, p. 26). Human chorionic gonadotropin staining does not establish choriocarcinoma: it also stains the syncytiotrophoblastic cells found in seminoma (Siegmund 2023, p. 38).
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, each rule verified against the printed page. Siegmund SE, Mehra R, Acosta AM. Human Pathology 2023;133:32-55 (online 2022): Table 1, p. 34; KIT and D2-40, p. 36; CD30, OCT3/4, SOX2 and SOX17, p. 37; glypican-3, alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin and HNF1-beta, p. 38. Wu 2020, Tables 1-2. Rougemont 2018, pp. 26, 29, 31, 33-35. Contract rules 1-5 are kept; rules 1, 3 and 5 carry negatives the contract's table did not, so a seminoma with focal CD30, or an embryonal carcinoma with CD117 or D2-40, does not take the other's code. With OCT3/4 positive, a positive SOX17 decides the panel for the germinoma family whatever CD30 or SOX2 show (rule 4; a panel with OCT3/4, SOX17 and CD30 fires it), because SOX17 is negative in every embryonal carcinoma (Siegmund p. 37). Without SOX17, a panel positive for CD30 and for CD117 or D2-40 is coded 9064/3 unless SOX2 settles it (rule 2): rule 0 records it for CD117, the fallback for D2-40. Contract rules 6-8 (one yolk sac marker each) are replaced by two pairs, OCT3/4 not positive in each: glypican-3 with alpha-fetoprotein, and glypican-3 with nuclear HNF1-beta. A single yolk sac marker falls to the fallback. The pair alpha-fetoprotein with HNF1-beta is not built: no source on disk reports the two stains on the same tumours (Rougemont did not stain alpha-fetoprotein, p. 28; Siegmund p. 38 compares their accuracy, not their co-expression). Residual risk, teratoma: glypican-3 stains 20-38% and tissue alpha-fetoprotein 0-27% of teratomas (Siegmund p. 38); nuclear HNF1-beta stains enteric-type teratoma glands in 11/16 (Rougemont p. 26; Table 5, p. 33); Wu Tables 1-2 found glypican-3 in 1/10 and alpha-fetoprotein in 2/10 mature teratomas, weak and in 2-3% of cells. No source reports how often a teratoma expresses both markers of a pair; one that does is coded 9071/3. Residual risk, choriocarcinoma: OCT3/4 negative and glypican-3 positive in 33-100% (Table 1, p. 34; p. 38); each pair needs a second marker the sources report choriocarcinoma rarely or never shows (alpha-fetoprotein, p. 38; nuclear HNF1-beta, Rougemont p. 26). SALL4 is declared and asked by no rule: it marks germ cell lineage, not type (Siegmund p. 36). Choriocarcinoma is not coded from immunohistochemistry (contract §4.2). Fallback 9064/3 per D2.

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and SOX2 are positive and SOX17 is not: the embryonal carcinoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, p. 37). Recorded as Embryonal carcinoma, NOS (9070/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 2. Siegmund 2023 p. 37 (Nonaka): diffuse SOX2 with negative SOX17 in 100% of embryonal carcinomas; diffuse SOX17 with negative SOX2 in 100% of seminomas. SOX2 in teratoma epithelium (up to 81%) is excluded by OCT3/4, which teratoma lacks (Table 1, p. 34). Listed first: it emits rule 1's code, and above rule 0 it keeps SOX2 asked before rule 0 can settle.

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4, CD30 and CD117 are all positive, and SOX2 and SOX17 are not: the panel matches neither the embryonal carcinoma pattern (CD30 without CD117) nor the seminoma pattern (CD117 without CD30) (Siegmund 2023, p. 37), so it does not establish the germ cell tumour's type. Recorded as Germinoma (9064/3): ICD-O-3.2 files Germ cell tumor, NOS under this number, so the record does not assert that a germinoma was diagnosed.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 0, after rule 2 and ahead of rule 1, so the flow asks CD117 before rule 1 can settle and SOX2 before rule 0 can. The engine counts an unasked negative marker as off and stops at the first satisfied rule, asking only about rules above it, so without this rule a seminoma with focal CD30 and a positive CD117 the clerk was never asked about was coded 9070/3. It records what the node's fallback records for the same panel; SOX2 and SOX17 negative keep rules 2 and 4 deciding when either is positive. Siegmund 2023 p. 37: CD30+/KIT- is 100% specific for embryonal carcinoma and CD30-/KIT+ for seminoma (Leroy).

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and CD30 are positive, and the seminoma markers CD117 and SOX17 are not: the embryonal carcinoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, p. 37). Recorded as Embryonal carcinoma, NOS (9070/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 1. Siegmund 2023 p. 37: CD30 stains embryonal carcinoma (83-100%) and focally stains 0-50% of seminomas; CD30+/KIT- is 100% specific for embryonal carcinoma (Leroy). OCT3/4 marks seminoma and embryonal carcinoma (100% each, p. 37). negative CD117 and SOX17: added to the contract's rule, so a seminoma with focal CD30 is not coded embryonal carcinoma. SOX17 is negative in 100% of embryonal carcinomas (Nonaka, p. 37).

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and CD117 are positive and CD30 is not: the seminoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, pp. 36-37). Dysgerminoma, seminoma and germinoma are one tumour under three names (Moch 2022, p. 464), and the name this site uses is recorded. Recorded as Germinoma (9064/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 3. Siegmund 2023 p. 36: KIT stains 88-100% of seminomas; focal cytoplasmic KIT occurs in 32-44% of non-seminomatous tumours. p. 37: CD30-/KIT+ is 100% specific for seminoma (Leroy). negative CD30: added to the contract's rule for the same reason as rule 1. Family code by site, D3.

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and SOX17 are positive: the seminoma pattern. Embryonal carcinoma does not express SOX17 (Siegmund 2023, p. 37). Dysgerminoma, seminoma and germinoma are one tumour under three names (Moch 2022, p. 464), and the name this site uses is recorded. Recorded as Germinoma (9064/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 4. Siegmund 2023 p. 37 (Nonaka): SOX17 diffuse in 100% of seminomas, negative in 100% of embryonal carcinomas and in choriocarcinoma; variable in yolk sac tumour and teratoma, both OCT3/4 negative (Table 1, p. 34). No CD30 negative: a panel with OCT3/4, SOX17 and CD30 positive fires this rule (rule 1 requires SOX17 not positive), because SOX17 is negative in every embryonal carcinoma and CD30 focally stains up to half of seminomas (p. 37).

resolution_logic.reason: OCT3/4 and D2-40 are positive and CD30 is not: the seminoma pattern (Siegmund 2023, pp. 36-37). Dysgerminoma, seminoma and germinoma are one tumour under three names (Moch 2022, p. 464), and the name this site uses is recorded. Recorded as Germinoma (9064/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 5. Siegmund 2023 p. 36: D2-40 strongly stains up to 100% of seminomas; embryonal carcinoma stains in 0-69%, focally. negative CD30: added to the contract's rule, so focal D2-40 in an embryonal carcinoma does not read as seminoma. p. 37: KIT/D2-40/SOX17 mark seminoma, CD30/SOX2 embryonal carcinoma.

resolution_logic.reason: Glypican-3 and alpha-fetoprotein both stain the tumour and OCT3/4 is not positive: the yolk sac tumour pattern (Siegmund 2023, p. 38; Wu 2020, Tables 1-2). Recorded as Yolk sac tumor, NOS (9071/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 6. Siegmund 2023 p. 38: glypican-3 in 100% of yolk sac tumours and tissue alpha-fetoprotein in 55-100%; a subset of yolk sac tumours co-expresses alpha-fetoprotein and glypican-3 (Nogales). Choriocarcinoma, glypican-3 positive in 33-100%, is rarely alpha-fetoprotein positive (p. 38; Table 1, p. 34). Wu P, et al. Pediatr Surg Int 2020 (doi:10.1007/s00383-020-04652-w; the PDF prints no page numbers), Tables 1-2: alpha-fetoprotein 21/22 and glypican-3 22/22 paediatric yolk sac tumours. OCT3/4 negative in yolk sac tumour, Table 1, p. 34.

resolution_logic.reason: Glypican-3 and nuclear HNF1-beta are positive and OCT3/4 is not: the yolk sac tumour pattern (Rougemont 2018, Table 2, p. 29). Recorded as Yolk sac tumor, NOS (9071/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Rule 7. Rougemont AL, Tille JC. Human Pathology 2018;81:26-36: Table 2, p. 29, glypican-3 positive in 42 of the 44 nuclear HNF1-beta positive yolk sac components it lists; p. 34, glypican-3 positive in 43/45; p. 35, recommends a panel combining SALL4, HNF1-beta, glypican-3 and OCT4. Choriocarcinoma shows cytoplasmic HNF1-beta only, never nuclear (p. 26; Table 5, p. 33), so the nuclear stain excludes it. p. 31: every yolk sac tumour SALL4 positive and OCT4 negative.
